issues: [reviewer] index.html — 'Crowd favorites' cards: every card reuses the exact same coffee-cup SVG (Espresso & Pour-Overs, Seasonal Specials, Fresh Pastries, Beans to Take Home all share one glyph). Divergent services get zero visual distinction and the menu reads templated. Fix: give each a distinct glyph (croissant, bean bag, pour-over dripper, catering tray) or drop icons and let the Fraunces headings carry it.

[reviewer] index.html — about section paragraph: 'The neighborhood spot for Cafe at 3805 Maltby Rd, Bothell, WA 98012' has a category-template artifact ('for Cafe') that reads as filler mid-sentence. Fix: rewrite to 'The neighborhood cafe at 3805 Maltby Rd…' or drop 'for Cafe' entirely.

[reviewer] styles.css — hero h1 (.hero--editorial-asymmetric h1 clamp up to 4.2rem): the name and the offer share one inline line, so at ~360px the gradient span 'Freshly brewed in the neighborhood' wraps unpredictably mid-phrase and renders as a second full-voltage heading line competing with the name. Fix: make .accent display:block (or give it a smaller, muted size) so the offer is clearly subordinate to 'Ridge Coffee'.

praise: Palette is disciplined and business-specific: one warm coffee-brown family plus a single gold accent carried through hero, cards, stats, banner, footer — coordinated, not gradient soup.
Type pairing is confident: Fraunces display vs Inter body with clamp() scale and tight tracking; no system-font fallback aroma.

Hierarchy and one-visit test pass: name → offer → single primary 'Call (425) 481-8801' CTA, reinforced in topbar, header, hero, about card, banner, and footer; a visitor can name the business, what it does, and how to reach it in seconds.
Copy is specific and believable — real street address, '4.6 · 93 Google reviews', 'Takeout ready in about 15 minutes' — with no lorem or 'welcome to our website' filler.
